payload.name: Preserve Separate Memories for Struggle and Success
payload.description: Use when a construction candidate or memory decision involves a single message that explicitly reports both a difficulty/struggle and a positive outcome/achievement, to avoid losing the positive fact by merging.
content: During extraction, keep both the challenge and the positive outcome in the candidate content when a single message explicitly states both. During CRUD, do not merge them into one memory that records only the struggle; create separate memories (e.g., one event for the challenge, one event for the achievement) unless the positive statement is not a real result.

Split only when both facets are explicitly supported by the message. If the message states only one facet, or the positive wording is a future plan, preference, or neutral comment rather than a result, keep a single memory to avoid over-splitting.

candidates.solves: Fixes construction losing an explicitly stated positive outcome when the same message also reports a struggle, because both are collapsed into one memory that keeps only the struggle. Applies to future messages where one utterance explicitly reports both a difficulty and an achievement/positive result; create separate memories. Not applicable when the message only has one facet or the positive wording is a plan/preference/neutral comment rather than a real result.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated items during extraction
payload.description: When a source message lists multiple distinct traits, reasons, or motivations (joined by 'and' or commas), keep every listed item in extraction candidates and any memory update; do not drop an item unless it restates the same fact.
content: During extraction, when a message states several distinct facts in a list or conjunction (e.g., 'passionate about A and B' or 'because of X, Y, and Z'), preserve every enumerated item in the candidate; do not omit an item as redundant unless the speaker's wording clearly restates a single fact.

During CRUD, when an ADD or UPDATE targets a memory that lacks one of the items enumerated in the source message, include the missing item in the new or merged content; never let a later version drop a detail that remains supported by evidence.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes summarize away one item from an enumerated list of traits, reasons, or motivations, so later memory cannot answer questions about the dropped item. This Skill applies whenever a future message lists multiple distinct attributes or motives that should all be recorded; it does not apply when the listed items are redundant paraphrases of a single fact or when the message contains no enumerable facts.

payload.name: Preserve all explicitly enumerated facts about an object
payload.description: When a user message explicitly lists multiple purposes, functions, uses, or attributes of a single object or plan and a memory candidate is being extracted or updated from that message.
content: If one message explicitly enumerates several purposes, uses, or attributes of the same object or plan, include every enumerated item in the candidate; do not keep only one item or summarize away the rest.
Name the object exactly as the evidence names it; do not replace it with a different object inferred from context.
When updating an existing memory with an explicit list, preserve the full list from the new evidence while still removing facts the new evidence contradicts.

candidates.solves: Memory construction can fail when a candidate summary drops some of several explicitly enumerated facts about an object or plan, or when it substitutes a different object than the one named in the evidence. This Skill applies to future sessions where one message lists multiple purposes, uses, functions, or attributes of the same item and that message is the source for extraction or update. It does not apply when the message makes a single general claim, when the message concerns separate unrelated objects, or when an existing memory is merely reworded without introducing a new enumerated list.

payload.name: Extract distinct facts per message during candidate generation
payload.description: When extracting candidates from a session and a later user message contains a new durable fact about a subject already mentioned in an earlier message, extract that fact as its own candidate instead of reusing or extending the earlier candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, treat each user message independently: identify every durable fact it states, even if the same subject or vehicle appears in an earlier message.

If a later message adds a distinct event or state (e.g., an item breaking down, a purchase, an accident) not present in the earlier extraction, create a separate candidate for it rather than reusing or merging it into the candidate from the earlier message.
Do not create duplicate candidates when the later message only restates or elaborates a fact already captured in an earlier candidate.

candidates.solves: During candidate extraction, distinct durable facts from different user messages in the same session can be collapsed into one candidate, so a later message's new fact (e.g., an item breaking down) never becomes a memory. This Skill applies when a later user message states a new event or state about a subject already mentioned earlier in the same session, and extraction may reuse an earlier candidate. It does not apply when the later message merely restates or elaborates a fact already captured in an earlier candidate.

payload.name: ExtractEachDistinctFactAsSeparateCandidate
payload.description: When a single message contains both an already-known fact and a new distinct fact (especially a purchase/event with a relative time), split them into separate extraction candidates; do not let the known fact absorb the new one.
content: During candidate extraction, emit one candidate per distinct factual claim in a message; do not bundle a new event/purchase under an already-known ownership or state fact.

Before SKIPping any candidate because its subject is already in memory, check the full message for another claim carrying new information (e.g., a purchase with a relative time); if found, create a separate candidate for that new fact and resolve its relative time to the concrete date from the message timestamp.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes bundles a new fact (e.g., a purchase with a relative date) into a candidate whose dominant claim is already known, causing a legitimate SKIP that silently drops the new fact. The Skill applies when a future message restates an already-memorized fact in the same sentence or turn as a distinct new event/purchase; it requires emitting one candidate per distinct claim so the new fact survives. It must not apply to messages that contain only a single claim or to candidates that genuinely add no new information, where SKIP remains correct.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicitly Enumerated Items in Extraction
payload.description: When extracting memories from a message that explicitly enumerates multiple distinct reasons, strategies, preferences, or steps, preserve every listed item and do not add any unlisted detail.
content: When a source message explicitly lists multiple distinct items (reasons, strategies, preferences, steps), create one candidate per listed item, or one candidate containing the complete explicit list; never drop a listed item.
Before accepting the candidate, compare it against the source: every distinct item in the enumeration must be represented; if any is missing, revise the candidate.
Do not add any strategy, reason, preference, or activity that is not stated in the source message.

candidates.solves: When a speaker explicitly lists multiple distinct reasons, strategies, preferences, or steps in one message, extraction tends to drop one listed item and may invent an unsupported one. This applies to future messages with explicit enumerations; preserve every listed item and add nothing unlisted. Not for single-fact messages or implied inferences.

payload.name: extract_ordinal_enumerated_traits
payload.description: When a user message lists multiple entities with ordinal labels (oldest, second, third, youngest, etc.) and assigns each a distinct personality or attribute, extract one memory candidate per entity during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message enumerates entities using ordinal descriptors (oldest, second, third, youngest, etc.) and gives each its own attribute, create one separate candidate per enumerated item.
Each candidate must preserve the entity type (e.g., pet, fur baby), the ordinal/positional descriptor, and the stated trait or attribute for that specific item.
Do not create per-item candidates for general group statements that do not assign distinct attributes to each enumerated member; stop after the explicitly enumerated items.

candidates.solves: The construction extractor omits candidates when a single user message enumerates several distinct items with ordinal labels (e.g., oldest, second, third, youngest) and assigns each a separate attribute, so all those facts are lost. The skill applies when such an ordinal enumeration appears in one message and each item has its own trait. It does not apply to group-level statements ('they are all playful') or to enumerations without per-item attributes.

payload.name: Extract-all-items-from-enumerated-statements
payload.description: Apply during candidate extraction when a single speaker message enumerates multiple distinct durable facts of the same category (e.g., activities, events, preferences, goals); capture each listed item so no stated fact is dropped.
content: During candidate extraction, if a message lists multiple distinct durable facts of the same category (e.g., 'studying, attending workshops, and networking'), create one candidate per listed item, or a single candidate that explicitly names every listed item; do not extract only the first or most salient item.
Limit extraction to the items actually asserted in the message; do not infer additional facts, complete partial lists, or expand the enumeration beyond what the speaker stated.

candidates.solves: Extraction frequently collapses an enumerated list in one message into a single candidate that captures only the most salient item, leaving other stated durable facts missing from memory. This Skill applies when a future message explicitly lists multiple distinct facts of the same category (activities, events, preferences, goals) that all merit memory; it requires capturing each item. It must not apply to messages where listed items are illustrative examples or where only one item is asserted as a durable fact, and it does not require exhaustive expansion beyond the speaker's own enumeration.
